tp-collections-test: JE StoredIterator holds a live write-locked cursor across iterator.set() so two crossed iterators deadlock and the runner retries/aborts. noxu collection iterators are construction-time SNAPSHOTS (documented deviation) that hold no cursor lock between next() calls, so the two-iterator deadlock is structurally impossible at this layer. The underlying lock-conflict/deadlock-detection engine behaviour is COVERED-CITED in noxu-db isolation_test.rs.

je_test_doc: Tests a bug when the BlockIterator repositioned at an earlier key when the last key in the previous block was deleted.
notes: tp-collections-test: regression for JE BlockIterator.repositionRange over a sorted-DUPLICATES DB (setIteratorBlockSize(5)); after deleting the last dup with a second live cursor the first cursor must not reposition to an earlier record. noxu collection iterators are snapshots with no BlockIterator/repositionRange machinery, and the collections layer exposes no block-size/duplicate-cursor knob, so the specific bug cannot recur here. Documented iterator-snapshot deviation.

tp-collections-test: JE joins storeMap.values()/keySet()/entrySet() against two secondary index maps via StoredCollection.join(). noxu-collections has no join() on its views (StoredMap wraps a primary only); the natural-join intersection over secondary indices is COVERED-CITED at the engine layer in noxu-db je_join_test.rs (JoinCursor). Collections-view join wrapper intentionally absent.

tp-collections-test: JE stores/reads a null value via a binding that supports null and rejects null with a binding/entity-binding that does not. noxu has no Java null; the null-supporting half maps to Option<T> (round-trips None) and the empty-slice value; the "reject null with a non-null base class / entity binding" half is a Java-binding-config detail with no Rust analogue (Option<T> either does or does not permit None at the type level).

tp-collections-test: JE crosses a primary put/delete thread (locks primary then secondary) with a secondary get thread (locks secondary then primary) to force the primary/secondary lock-ordering deadlock and verify the runner retries it. This is an engine lock-ordering/deadlock-detection property, not a collections-view property; the collection map-view merely forwards to Database/SecondaryDatabase. Engine deadlock detection + secondary lock behaviour are COVERED-CITED in noxu-db.
